knowledge_point.title: Finding a Scalar Factor in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
The arrows show $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b$, and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf c$. Solid grid lines are one unit apart; dotted lines divide each square in half.

![](images/39/3959019dd3372f24bf1f19f0c3d343d0bb646e13fc9565aa3a9e1a988b34f206.png)

Given that $\mathbf{c}=\frac{3}{2}\mathbf{a}+\lambda\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.

$\lambda=$ {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Construct the known component $\frac{3}{2}\mathbf{a}$ from $O$, and call its endpoint $P$. Count signed horizontal and vertical grid displacements:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OP} &=\frac{3}{2}\,(3, -2)=\left(\frac{9}{2}, -3\right). \\
\overrightarrow{PC} &=(2, -2).
\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/b8/b868f394ca53282f46097fc5bca2e2431db99bda2382cc3e2a1b0879c55760da.png)

Compare the remaining displacement with $\mathbf{b}$, whose grid displacement is $(4, -4)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Horizontal scale} &=\frac{2}{4}=\frac{1}{2} \\
\text{Vertical scale} &=\frac{-2}{-4}=\frac{1}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

The scale is positive, so the remaining vector has the same direction as $\mathbf{b}$. Thus $\overrightarrow{PC}=\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{b}$. By the triangle law,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c} &=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC} \\
&=\frac{3}{2}\mathbf{a}+\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{b} \\
&=\frac{3}{2}\mathbf{a}+\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are not parallel, so their coefficients are unique. Matching the coefficient of $\mathbf{b}$ gives $\lambda=\frac{1}{2}$.

conversions: Reduce grid displacement ratio to a positive rational scalar
